stem: Data sets P, Q and R each contain 6 values. P: \(10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 20\); Q: \(10, 15, 15, 15, 15, 20\); R: \(10, 10, 15, 15, 20, 20\). Which list orders the data sets from least to greatest standard deviation?

choices.C: The three standard deviations are equal.

solution: All three data sets have a mean of 15 and a range of 10, so compare the distances from 15.
Q has four values at the mean (distance 0) and two at distance 5. R has two values at the mean and four at distance 5. P has all six values at distance 5.
So the spread increases from Q to R to P.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the order. The values of P are all 5 away from the mean, which is the most spread out, not the least.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Q has more values at the mean than R, so Q is less spread out than R.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The data sets have the same mean and the same range, but their values are at different distances from the mean, so the standard deviations differ.
explanation.D: Correct. Q has the most values at the mean, R has fewer, and P has none, so the standard deviations increase in the order Q, R, P.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
sd = lambda d: sqrt(sum((x - Rational(sum(d), len(d)))**2 for x in d) / len(d))
ssd = lambda d: sqrt(sum((x - Rational(sum(d), len(d)))**2 for x in d) / (len(d) - 1))
P = [10, 10, 10, 20, 20, 20]
Q = [10, 15, 15, 15, 15, 20]
R = [10, 10, 15, 15, 20, 20]
assert sum(P) == sum(Q) == sum(R) and max(P) - min(P) == max(Q) - min(Q) == max(R) - min(R)
for f in (sd, ssd):
    assert f(Q) < f(R) < f(P)
assert choices[answer] == 'Q, R, P'
